54ce4f003f0d.title: Critical security vulnerability affects OpenSSH on Alpine Linux systems
54ce4f003f0d.hook_fa: این خبر چه تغییری برای کاربران لینوکس ایجاد می‌کند؟
54ce4f003f0d.description: Version 10.6p2 of OpenSSH has been released with a workaround for a critical vulnerability that affects Linux systems that use musl libc with PAM disabled, such as Alpine Linux . OpenSSH developer Damien Miller said : If you operate a Linux system that uses musl libc without PAM (Alpine Linux is one example) then stop reading and set PasswordAuthentication=no or disable SSH for these systems IMMEDIATELY. This vulnerability does not exist on non-Linux systems, Linux/glibc systems and Linux systems that use PAM for password authentication. We consider the root cause of this bug to be outside OpenSSH itself, but we're in a good position to deliver a mitigation quickly. The Alpine Linux project has announced that it will be backporting the OpenSSH fix " all the way back to Alpine 3.16 ", which was released in May 2022.

1f0fbd83c5ab.description: When a computer hibernates, the kernel writes the contents of memory to disk and then shuts the system down. Resuming from hibernation involves reading that data back into memory, and then having the kernel pick up where it left off. Unfortunately, the kernel does not have any way to know that the data it is reading back has not been tampered with, which is why lockdown , an optional kernel feature that attempts to prevent modifications to the running kernel, disables hibernation. Matthew Garrett, who has been working on lockdown for many years, has shared a patch set that aims to fix this problem. His solution must also protect against downgrade attacks (where an attacker reboots the computer with an older kernel version to bypass new protections), which complicates the implementation.

59ce2f9cf2d0.description: The Node.js project recently had a security vulnerability that affected its Brotli decoder. The bug was a buffer overflow , but the particular way that official Node.js binaries are built for Linux meant that one of the main protections against turning a buffer overflow into remote code execution, address space layout randomization (ASLR) could not be turned on. If ASLR had been enabled, the bug would still be exploitable in theory, but much more difficult to exploit in practice. In response, the GNU C Library (glibc) is considering a new set of tunable settings to allow administrators to forbid programs that do not support ASLR. The new settings, while a welcome hardening measure, may not address the root problem.

2d77cabeef0c.description: Patrick Garrity of VulnCheck has written a blog post that looks at vulnerabilities found by Anthropic's Project Glasswing since it launched on April 7, and finds it wanting: Of the 37,966 findings Anthropic reports, only 7,349 (19.4%) have been made public. Just 217 of those have been marked fixed. The more glaring number is that 4.4% (1,654) of the project's findings have already been marked as duplicates, 7.5x more duplicates than fixes. On top of that, 419 findings have been withdrawn. It seems odd that the ledger now claims a 94.2% true positive rate, up from 90.8% at launch, when more findings have been withdrawn or marked as duplicates than fixed, likely a feedback loop missing to the triage rates listed as "True Positives". [...] AI is a valuable tool for finding vulnerabilities, and I'm not discounting that. But seven months in, the evidence still doesn't match the launch narrative. The CVEs are a sliver of this year's total, almost none are being exploited, fixes have stalled while duplicates and withdrawals pile up, and the triage burden is shifting onto the open source maintainers Glasswing promised to help. The receipts keep coming in. They still don't reconcile.

0cbee04adb87.description: Christoph Hellwig has announced the initial public release of XRAID—declustered parity RAID that is integrated into XFS. The two primary aims of XRAID are to support parity RAID on zoned devices like SMR hard drives, and to provide a fast RAID implementation without inherent data integrity problems. XRAID, just like zoned XFS also works on conventional hard drives and SSDs. Optimizing for SSD performance has not been a focus, but even without that, writes are up to 20 times faster than mdraid. [...] Work on XRAID has been ongoing for a year and a half, and while we aren't anywhere near ready for an upstream submission, we are interested in feedback and testing from a wider audience now. The current implementation supports zero to 2 parities. We did experiments with the SnapRAID parity library to support 3 and more parities, and while that is not included in the current version, support for more parities is planned and the code is prepared for it. The xfsprogs branch includes mkfs support and a new "xraid" utility for managing devices and inspecting an XRAID file-systems. 8d452d3d153d.description: Drew DeVault has announced that Redict , a fork of Redis that was created in response to Redis's 2024 license change , has been deprecated. He recommends switching to Valkey , the permissively licensed Redis fork supported by the Linux Foundation. The two projects are mutually compatible, so switching should be as simple as changing which package is installed and renaming the configuration file. I had hoped to rally the Redis diaspora around a copyleft initiative, to protect ourselves from future rug-pulls, and made Redict to serve this purpose. However, with the valkey project's success, and Redis's return to a copyleft license, Redict was not able to build a sustainable community. We recommend that Redict users switch to valkey, which uses a permissive license but has better long-term prospects. We advise against switching back to Redis; though it is once again open source, and copyleft, it uses a contributor license agreement which will facilitate another rug-pull when Redis has a bad financial quarter.

The worst flaw, it says, would allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute commands on an affected nginx server with HTTP/2 enabled . The company also reports a local-privilege escalation (LPE) kernel vulnerability , which was introduced in the 4.15 kernel, in the Stream Control Transmission Protocol (SCTP) subsystem. If chained with the NGINX vulnerability, it would allow an attacker to gain root privileges on the host. A kernel patch for this is not yet available. We also obtained a root shell on the host in a setup where nginx was running in a Docker container. On many Linux distributions, the SCTP module is installed by default and the kernel loads it automatically the first time a program opens an SCTP socket. 0a2c61cf0868.description: The BPF verifier has historically worked by tracing every possible path of execution through a program, checking, at each instruction, that various safety properties hold. This works, but it can result in an exponential increase in the number of states that need checking in programs with complicated control-flow. Alexei Starovoitov, one of the kernel's core BPF maintainers, has shared a patch set that substantially reworks how the verifier tracks states, in order to reduce the size of that exponential explosion.
